question: Using properties of determinants, prove that $$\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\a & b & c\\bc & ca & ab\end{vmatrix}=(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)$$ and hence evaluate the determinant for $a=2$, $b=-1$, and $c=4$.
explanation:
Applying column operations
Let
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\a & b & c\\bc & ca & ab\end{vmatrix}$$
Apply $C_2\to C_2-C_1$ and $C_3\to C_3-C_1$. These operations do not change the value of the determinant.
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 & 0\\a & b-a & c-a\\bc & ca-bc & ab-bc\end{vmatrix}$$
Expanding along the first row,
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}b-a & c-a\\ca-bc & ab-bc\end{vmatrix}$$
Factorising the elements of the second row,
$$ca-bc=c(a-b),\quad ab-bc=b(a-c)$$
Therefore,
$$D=(b-a)b(a-c)-(c-a)c(a-b)$$
Using $b-a=-(a-b)$ and $a-c=-(c-a)$,
$$D=(a-b)b(c-a)-(a-b)c(c-a)$$
$$D=(a-b)(c-a)(b-c)$$
Hence,
$$D=(a-b)(b-c)(c-a)$$

Evaluation
For $a=2$, $b=-1$, and $c=4$,
$$D=(2+1)(-1-4)(4-2)$$
$$D=3(-5)(2)=-30$$
Therefore, the value of the determinant is $-30$.
